museum_text.zh: 1080年蘇軾謫居黃州（湖北黃岡），第三年（1082）四月寒食日，有感於季節更替，生活困乏，及仕途的挫折，作〈寒食雨二首〉，後來書成此卷，將詩中所描寫的心境，轉化成筆墨變化豐富的書法形象，詩中抑鬱的情感如決堤般從筆端傾洩而下。此卷由宋至今，流傳九百餘年，後人譽為蘇軾最好的書法傑作。 蘇軾（1037－1101），四川眉山人。嘉祐二年（1057）進士。他兼善詩文、繪畫、書法，與蔡襄、黃庭堅、米芾並稱北宋四大書家。
museum_text.en:
Su Shih was a native of Szechwan also known by his sobriquet Tung-po and an outstanding calligrapher, statesman, and writer of the Sung.

This handscroll of two poems was written in 1082. In these two poems, Su reveals how he ran afoul of court politics and was exiled to Huang-chou, Hupeh. His calligraphy flows with strong emotions as the strokes rise and fall according to his feelings and as the characters increase in size to a crescendo. In writing, Su was not technically adept at suspending the wrist but very gifted at free writing with great individuality. His characters are expansive, strokes strong and deep, and ink jet-black, creating for a new realm of expressiveness in calligraphy at the time.

intro.zh: 苏轼是宋代杰出的书法家、政治家和文学家，1080年被贬到黄州。
intro.en: Su Shi, an outstanding calligrapher, statesman and writer of the Song, was exiled to Huangzhou in 1080.

intro.zh: 在那里的第三年（1082）四月寒食节，他有感于季节更替、生活困乏和仕途挫折，写下《寒食雨二首》，后来书成此卷。
intro.en: In the fourth month of his third year there, 1082, at the Cold Food Festival, he wrote two poems on the rain, the hardship of his life and his frustrations in office, and later wrote them out on this scroll.

intro.zh: 馆方说，笔画随着他的情绪起伏，字也越写越大，形成高潮。
intro.en: The museum describes the strokes rising and falling with his feelings, and the characters growing in size to a crescendo.

intro.zh: 后人称它为苏轼传世书法中最好的一件。
intro.en: Later critics praised it as Su Shi's finest surviving calligraphy.

look_for.zh: 这一段里写得很大的“破灶烧湿苇”几个字。
look_for.en: In this section, the large characters 破竈燒濕葦 ('a broken stove, burning wet reeds').

look_for.zh: 字的大小和间距随情绪有节奏地变化。
look_for.en: How the size of the characters and the spaces between them vary rhythmically with his emotions.

look_for.zh: 字形舒展，笔画厚重，墨色乌黑。
look_for.en: Expansive characters, strong deep strokes and jet-black ink.

look_for.zh: 卷末有他的朋友黄庭坚的题跋，字比苏轼的还大（这一段里看不到）。
look_for.en: At the end of the scroll, a colophon by his friend Huang Tingjian, in characters even larger than Su's (not in this section).

alt.zh: 手卷中的一段：泛黄纸上一列列粗重的黑色行书，有几个字比其他字大得多，还有红色印章。
alt.en: A section of a handscroll in bold running-script calligraphy: columns of black characters on yellowed paper, a few much larger than the rest, with red seals.

image_choice.note: One section: the poem's climax. The museum photographs this scroll in sections.

views.zh: 据馆方的英译，他说自己的字从短到长、从肥到瘦，什么样子都有。
views.en: In the museum's translation, he said his writing ranged from short to long and plump to bony.

quote.en: everything from short to long, plump to bony

about.zh: 诗人、书法家，苏轼的朋友

views.zh: 约1100年，他在卷末写下题跋；馆方说他谦称自己是在苏轼身后才受到瞩目。
views.en: Around 1100 he added a colophon at the end of the scroll; the museum says he humbly claimed he came into the spotlight only after Su's passing.
